gc_grt123_lung_cancer.label: CT Lung cancer risk prediction
gc_grt123_lung_cancer.description: This algorithm analyzes non-contrast CT scans of the thorax and predicts the lung cancer risk. The model consists of two modules. The first one is a 3D region proposal network for nodule detection, which outputs all suspicious nodules for a subject. The second one selects the top five nodules based on the detection confidence, evaluates their cancer probabilities and combines them with a leaky noisy-or gate to obtain the probability of lung cancer for the subject. This model was the winner of the Data Science Bowl 2017 competition hosted on Kaggle.
predictions: Lung thorax cancer nodule probability score
gc_grt123_lung_cancer.cite: F. Liao, M. Liang, Z. Li, X. Hu and S. Song, 'Evaluate the Malignancy of Pulmonary Nodules Using the 3D Deep Leaky Noisy-or Network', in IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, vol. 30, no. 11, pp. 3484-3495, Nov. 2019, doi: 10.1109/TNNLS.2019.2892409.

gc_autopet_fpr.label: Second place in AutoPET challenge: False Positive Reduction Network
gc_autopet_fpr.description: This algorithm segments tumor lesions in whole-body FDG-PET/CT. To prevent over-segmenting tumor regions due to high-uptake organs or inflammations, the model uses a false positive reduction network. First a self-supervised pre-trained global segmentation module coarsely delineates the candidate tumor regions using a self-supervised pre-trained encoder. The candidate tumor regions are then refined by removing false positives via a local refinement module.
gc_autopet_fpr.cite: Y. Peng, J. Kim, D. Feng and L. Bi, 'Automatic Tumor Segmentation via False Positive Reduction Network for Whole-Body Multi-Modal PET/CT Images', In arXiv:2209.07705, doi: 10.48550/arXiv:2209.07705.
